knownLimitation.statement: The defect is established by direct reproduction; its cause is not. What is established: under the system-chrome project on macOS at six workers, a 94-test run reported every test passing and then exited 1 because worker-3 was force-killed at the 300000ms teardown budget, after 342 seconds of wall time; the identical command exited 0 in 77 seconds on the preceding attempt, so the condition is intermittent; the bundled chromium project ran the identical set in 18.2s and exited 0; the two projects differ only in channel: chrome; the condition is absent at one worker, where the two projects differ by about a second; the stall occurs at release rather than during execution, since all 94 passes were reported first; the slowdown is standing at roughly four to one even when the run exits 0; and the condition does not reproduce in the pipeline, whose run accounts for all 708 of its tests. What is NOT established: the mechanism, which of four candidates applies, the frequency, a concurrency threshold, whether more than one worker can be affected, and the carried-in attribution to Chromium's CDP transport over --remote-debugging-pipe, for which no handle trace was taken here.

executionHistory.note: Reproduced the defect rather than recording it on report. Five Playwright runs in one session with the browser project as the only variable: the bundled chromium project ran 94 tests in 18.2s exiting 0, while the system-chrome project ran the identical set twice — once in 77 seconds exiting 0, and once in 342 seconds with 'Error: worker-3 process did not exit within 300000ms after stop, force-killed it' and exit 1, every test passing in all three. All output was written outside the repository and nothing was modified. Filed SEPARATELY from BUG-016 and explicitly not merged with it: pipeline run 32651572136 accounts for all 708 of its tests as passes or failures, so no teardown loss occurred there and this defect cannot explain that red gate. Three reported characteristics were not reproduced and are recorded as such: three to six force-killed workers (exactly one, worker-3, was observed), an 88-test suite (94 were run), and the CDP --remote-debugging-pipe attribution (no handle trace taken here, recorded as a candidate only). Two findings go beyond the report: the slowdown is standing at roughly four to one even on a clean exit-0 run, and the condition is absent at one worker, which is why a single-spec reproduction attempt does not find it.
